title: Prayer: A Dialogue of Hearts Blossoming with Love
summary:
Imagine your seven or eight-year-old child, running around the house, laughing one moment and grumbling the next, then hearing the call to prayer. They might slow down, and perhaps wonder internally: "Do I have to pray now?" At this age, your child begins to understand that prayer is an obligation, but they might see it as a burden or a heavy task, especially with their preoccupation with play and exploring the world around them. You are not a coach imposing orders here, but a loving guide opening doors of love and tranquility for them.

The key is combining gentleness with consistently instructing the child to pray once they reach age seven, while connecting their heart with Allah in a warm and beloved way. Prayer is not just movements; it is a daily intimate conversation with our Lord, an opportunity for calm and reflection, and a source of strength and reassurance. When your child sees prayer in you as love and longing, and not just a habit or an obligation, their heart will begin to incline towards it. Always remember the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not make people flee.» (Sahih al-Bukhari 69). This is our approach to raising our children to love prayer, with gentleness, kindness, and encouragement.

Start with a good example; make your prayer in front of them a model of humility and comfort. Talk to them about the beauty of prayer, about the stories of the prophets and righteous people and how their prayers were a light in their lives. Encourage them to participate with you, even if it's a simple participation, and celebrate every step they take towards it. The goal is for them to feel a sense of belonging to this great pillar of Islam, and to associate prayer with psychological comfort, not with coercion or reprimand.
try_this: Tonight: Pray Isha with your child, recite aloud in the first two units of prayer, then after the salutation, smile at them and say: "How wonderful it is to pray together, my dear!" Then ask them: "How many units of prayer did we pray?" without waiting for a correct answer, just to open a dialogue.
reflection_prompts: How did you feel while praying with your child tonight?
What did you notice about your child during or after the prayer?
parent_script: «Prayer is our intimate conversation with our Lord, my little one, and it draws us closer to Him and gives us peace of mind.»
